newsitem.title: UK: Panamaxes again lead Ldn freight higher.
newsitem.headline: Panamaxes again lead Ldn freight higher.

text.p: The advance of the Panamax sector to ever firmer levels which has been the strongest feature of the October freight market was extended on Wednesday.

A heavy volume of fixtures has been reported but brokers are more optimistic about rates gaining further ground in the Pacific than in the Atlantic. Despite evidence of more chartering enquiry for coal in the West brokers are less confident about prospects in this area. Much the same pattern applies for Capers.

The BFI rose 15 points to 1296 which included a sharp increase of 70 cents in the Caper Route 8, Queensland/Rotterdam coal. The North atlantic is strong for Handy-sizes but in most other areas dull conditions prevail for these types.

The US Gulf is a healthy market for owners of Panamaxes and Handies but although Panamax rates are very steady there is no great optimism that they may go significantly higher. Not a great deal of new grain busiss was seen Wednesday although Glencore quoted 50,000 HSS US Gulf/China for Nov 5/20, Pioneer 44/50,000 54' S Brazil/Lisbon-Hamburg range for Nov 10/25, and Dreyfus 30,000/5 barley Teesport/Jeddah for Nov 10/20.

Early Panamaxes which had looked vulnerable in the Atlantic Tuesday were said to be in better demand -- Olympic Galaxy 64,000 dwt held firm $11,750 daily passing Gibraltar for a trip via US Gulf to the Far East and the 1971-built Captain Diamantis 68,847 dwt open prompt US Gulf was said tbe trading a trip Far East with S Korean charterers at $11,500 daily plus $225,000 bonus against $11,000 daily plus $200,000.

Giovanni Bottiglieri 75,236 dwt which Transfield have just fixed delivery prompt Continent for a trip via US Gulf to the Far East at $13,000 daily was put back on the market by charterers and said to be attracting offers in excess of this level as a re-let. An illustration of the strength of the US Gulf for Handies was Strategic Bulkcarriers fixture of the 1977-built CTOR 27,700 dwt delivery SW pass Nov 6/12 for a trip with wheat to Tallinn redelivery passing Bornholm at $8,000 daily.

Brokers reported a shortage of Capers in the Far East. Panamaxes were in great demand and rates continued to move towards $11,000 daily for modern types for Pacific or Australian rounds. The 1995-built Eleranta 73,222 dwt, for example, was reported to be trading such business delivery Japan early Nov at $11,000 against charterer's $10,750 daily. The 16-built Atlantic Sovereign 68,641 dwt open Japan Nov 10/15 was being bid $10,250 daily for 3-5 months period timecharter with owners willing to accept $10,500.

Apart from the hot market for Handies in the US Gulf brokers also said scrap and steel charterers were increasingly active from the Continent. An economical modern 28,500 dwt craned bulker was seeing just below $10,000 daily delivery prompt Continent for a trip to the Far East. But S America and S Africa remain very weak.

IVS agreed a modest $4,500 daily on subjects delivery Durban for a trip to the Continent for a 1981-built 37,000 dwt vessel and J Lauritzen were said to have agreed a similar level for a 38,000 dwt geared vessel. In the Far East Vori 34,544 dwt was fixed for about 3 weeks local business at a respectable $7,250 daily. K Line were linked with a 42,000 dwt vessel Indonesia/Japan at about $7,500 daily, considered economical by brokers.-- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7729
